toegepas.voor: By 'n drom is dit die vel waarop jy geklop het wat vibreer.
toegepas.na: By 'n drom vibreer die vel waarop jy geklop het.
toegepas.rede_vinder: Two stacked relative clauses ('waarop ... wat vibreer') make the sentence hard to parse for Grade 4; the plain main-clause order says the same thing.
toegepas.fout: An English-style cleft ('dit is die vel ... wat vibreer') with two stacked relative clauses makes a Grade 4 reader stumble.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The plain main-clause order says the same thing (same part, same action, contrast with the guitar string intact) and reads more easily, and the next sentence still follows from it.

toegepas.voor: klop met jou hand op die vel
toegepas.na: klop met jou hand op die drom se vel
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'die vel' has no antecedent, because no skin has been mentioned yet; naming the drum makes the reference clear.
toegepas.fout: 'die vel' has no antecedent here; the drum is mentioned but its skin is not, so a child can read it as their own skin.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Naming the drum adds no new fact, since the drum is already in the paragraph, and it removes a real ambiguity; no protected wording is touched.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: met 'n dun stingel gras of riet
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Stingel gras' calques English 'stalk of grass'; Afrikaans forms the compound 'grasstingel', shortened with a hyphen before 'of'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: ''n Stingel gras' is the native Afrikaans measure construction, not a calque, and the elliptic hyphenated compound is harder for a Grade 4 reader.
